text: Hello, I am Dr. Agent. To help me understand your condition, can you describe the appearance of the rash on your scalp and forehead, and tell me if it is itchy, painful, or burning?

speaker: Patient
text: 3-month-old boy. The parents report that the rash has been present for several weeks, noting that it sometimes appears red and scaly, especially during cold weather. The patient was born at 36 weeks' gestation and has been generally healthy since. The patient's father has a history of psoriasis.

speaker: Doctor
text: Thank you for that information. Does the rash extend beyond the hairline onto the face or neck, and have you noticed any crusting or "cradle cap" scaling on the scalp?

speaker: Patient
text: My main symptom is Rash on scalp and forehead. I also have Erythematous patches, Greasy yellow scales, Worse in cold weather.

speaker: Doctor
text: The presence of greasy yellow scales and erythematous patches in a 3-month-old is highly characteristic of infantile seborrheic dermatitis. I will confirm this clinical impression by examining the distribution further. Are there any signs of oozing, weeping, or secondary infection in the affected areas?

speaker: Patient
text: Past medical history: Premature birth (36 weeks), otherwise generally healthy. Family history of psoriasis. Social history: The patient is 3 months old, so the social history is not applicable.

speaker: Doctor
text:
The greasy yellow scales and erythematous patches in a 3-month-old are classic for infantile seborrheic dermatitis, distinct from psoriasis which typically presents with silvery scales. I am confident in this clinical diagnosis based on the presentation.

DIAGNOSIS READY: Infantile Seborrheic Dermatitis
